anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Composite definition: The database simultaneously suffers from stale or incomplete optimizer statistics, severe transaction-level lock contention, and host-level CPU saturation. Each root cause is independently harmful, but when they occur together they create a reinforcing feedback loop that degrades throughput and response time in a highly concurrent OLTP workload.

Combined anomalous phenomena: 1) Execution plans show large cardinality misestimates and select sub-optimal join orders or access paths, often choosing full scans or low-selectivity index probes. 2) Those plans increase the number of rows touched and the duration of data-modifying statements, inflating the lock footprint and prolonging lock hold times. 3) Concurrent sessions pile up in long blocker-waiter chains; deadlock reports, application timeouts, and rising lock-wait seconds are observed alongside surging CPU utilisation near 100 %. 4) The CPU run queue grows as sessions spin on latch/lock manager operations, while background statistics-update tasks and deadlock detectors compete for the same saturated cores. Symptoms become hard to attribute to a single layer because query plans, lock waits, and CPU pressure all appear as co-primary bottlenecks.

Causal chain: Stale statistics → cardinality misestimation → inefficient, work-expensive plans → longer statement execution and larger lock scopes → lock contention and deadlocks → increased context switching and spin-waiting in the lock manager → CPU saturation. The saturated CPUs in turn slow automatic statistics collection and prolong rollback or deadlock-victim cleanup, keeping statistics stale and locks held even longer, thereby amplifying both the contention and the compute bottleneck in a self-reinforcing cycle.

entry.official_description: Error registering transaction from session '%u' to wait for sync before execution.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with extended waiting, resource queues, unresponsive peers, or configured time limits being exceeded before the requested operation completes.
entry.solution_guidance: Check wait sources, blocking chains, network responsiveness, timeout settings, and whether resource contention is prolonging operation completion.
